reason: Crossing orbits should bring rocky planetesimals into contact, helping build planetary embryos.
expectation: I expect collisions or accumulation among the planetesimals, though the immediate result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Breaking a layered body could provide fragments, but I want to start with the planetesimals' orbital interactions.

effect: The orbit-crossing step produced several growing embryos, so I can now focus on their further growth.
reaction: It is satisfying to see repeated impacts build multiple embryos rather than a single planet immediately.
reason: Gravitational focusing should help the embryos gather more material.
expectation: I expect the embryos to grow as their gravity attracts passing bodies, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Adding rocky planetesimals also seems useful for growth, but I want to follow the gravitational focusing route first.

effect: Gravitational focusing produced a larger, strongly attracting embryo that can now gather rocky fragments.
reaction: The feedback between growing mass and faster accretion is interesting.
reason: Adding rocky fragments seems like a practical next step toward growing a rocky world.
expectation: I expect the embryo to incorporate the fragments and grow, though its exact identity is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The other embryos can also gather planetesimals, but I want to develop the strongly attracting embryo first.

effect: The rocky fragments identified the growing embryo as proto-Earth, which can now acquire water-bearing material.
reaction: It is satisfying to see Earth emerge from the accumulated debris.
reason: Water-bearing asteroid rock seems directly relevant to growing a volatile-bearing young Earth.
expectation: I expect proto-Earth to incorporate hydrated rock and gain some of its volatile inventory.

alternatives.reason: Growing another embryo also serves a goal, but I want to develop proto-Earth first.

effect: Proto-Earth has gained hydrogen-bearing material, but it is not yet necessarily cool or ocean-covered; I still need to pursue the remaining growth paths.

reason: Adding rocky planetesimals to the other embryos should help grow another rocky world.
expectation: I expect an embryo to grow through further rocky accretion, though its identity is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Breaking the layered planetesimal may provide other material, but growing another embryo directly addresses a goal.

effect: The second embryo is Theia, completing that goal; the remaining combination may advance proto-Earth.
reaction: Naming Theia while acknowledging its uncertain properties is helpful.

reaction: The connection to iron meteorites is interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the young Earth goal.
expectation: I expect proto-Earth to incorporate the metal-rich fragments while retaining some volatile material.

reaction: The uncertainty around the sources and timing of Earth's hydrogen is a useful qualification.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding hydrated rock to proto-Earth was most worthwhile: it connected asteroid material to Earth's volatile inventory while distinguishing hydrated rock from a surface ocean.

leastWorthwhile.text: Breaking the layered planetesimal was the least engaging passage because it was the only offered combination at that point, although the link to iron meteorites was interesting.

surprise.text: I was struck that hydrated material could join a hot growing Earth without implying a cool planet or an ocean.

arbitrary.text: The final metal-fragment combination felt somewhat prescribed because it was the only offered action, though its purpose in building Earth was clear.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the hypothetical Theia encounter develops and how the story connects the young Earth to the Moon.
